Subject: Request: longer retention for session indexes + SOC2 evidence for deletion

Hi Sofia,

Quick intro — I lead infrastructure at MediQuest. We are evaluating a private deployment of Redwood and have two closely related asks we need for procurement / security: 1) can we retain session transcripts and their derived search indexes for 180 days in our Private deployment (on-prem VPC) for troubleshooting and regulatory forensics, and 2) we need SOC 2 / SIG evidence showing the deletion workflow (how a tenant-level delete propagates to indexes and to any archived logs).

Specific concerns:
- If we allow indexing of session transcripts for search, how do you ensure subsequent deletion will remove both the raw transcripts and any derived search indexes or tokens?
- Are there audit logs proving deletion events (who/when) that can be exported to our SIEM?
- If we request an exception to your default retention TTL for our tenant, what contractual/operational controls do you require?

Can you point me to the specific evidence artifacts (SOC 2 control mappings, sample deletion attestations, and any policy excerpts) and tell me the technical mechanism for delete propagation? Procurement will need the docs by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Hsu

Subject: Re: Request: longer retention for session indexes + SOC2 evidence for deletion

Claire / Sofia — tech detail from runtime side. Key points below and attachments referenced.

1) Indexing model and delete propagation
- We materialize search indexes as per-tenant vector stores inside the Private runtime; they are not exported unless the customer explicitly requests an export.
- Deletion flow: tenant delete request triggers (a) mark-for-delete metadata flag, (b) asynchronous sweeper that removes objects from object storage, (c) KV/LLM cache purge, (d) index pruning and re-compact; final GC removes orphaned shards.
- We emit an audit event at each stage (mark, purge start, purge complete) with event IDs.

2) Retention configuration options
- Default: 30 days for session transcripts, 90 days for operational logs, 365 days for audit logs.
- Custom: for Private deployments we can increase the transcript TTL to 180d for a given tenant via configuration and a signed amendment to the DPA. That config change records a change-event in the audit trail.

3) Evidence artifacts we can provide (attached):
- redwood_retention_policy_excerpt.pdf (policy section + amendment process)
- log_retention_matrix.csv (where deletion events live and export endpoints)
- syslog-archive-sample.txt (example export of audit events for SIEM ingestion)
- delete-propagation-attestation-sample.pdf (template we sign after a test deletion)

4) Considerations if you export indexes out-of-band
- If MediQuest pulls a copy of the vector index into your own store, Redwood cannot delete those external copies. We can (a) include contractual restrictions and (b) provide a documented workflow for joint deletion validation.

I'll join the Wednesday sync. Recommend we include one engineering contact from your side to walk through a dry-run.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference

Hi all — from privacy/compliance perspective a couple of notes to make procurement happy: 

- Any tenant-level retention increase must be accompanied by a DPA amendment or a signed SOW that references the retention delta. That amendment should enumerate responsibilities for external exports (if any).
- We should include a clause that "delete propagation" includes derived artifacts (indexes, caches, exports initiated by Redwood) and define a verification window (e.g., 72 hours for purge completion).
- We can provide a signed attestation after we run a deletion exercise; the attestation will include event IDs and timestamps. See attached attestation template.

Operational ask for the test: please provide an admin account that can trigger a tenant-level delete in the test environment and a contact who can verify the index is inaccessible from MediQuest's side (if you manage your own store, you'll need to coordinate deletion there too).

I'll also flag this for our SOC 2 evidence pack so procurement sees the mapping to CC6 / CC7 controls.

— Olga Petrov
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Hi Claire / Procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal review, here is the proposed plan and deliverables to address your procurement/security asks:

Plan (high-level):
1) Configuration: Redwood will enable a tenant-specific transcript TTL of 180 days in your Private runtime. This will be recorded as a configuration change with an audit event (we'll share event IDs).
2) Contract: We will execute a short DPA amendment that notes the retention extension and the verification obligations for any external exports you may perform. Legal will share draft language.
3) Deletion validation: We will schedule a deletion dry-run in the staging environment. Redwood will:
   - Perform the tenant delete; capture event IDs for mark/purge/start/complete.
   - Provide a signed attestation PDF that lists timestamps and event IDs.
   - Provide syslog export of the deletion events for your SIEM ingestion.
4) Evidence artifacts (attached + link):
   - redwood_retention_policy_excerpt.pdf — excerpt + amendment process
   - log_retention_matrix.csv — where deletion events are logged and export endpoints
   - syslog-archive-sample.txt — sample export structure for SIEM
   - delete-propagation-attestation-sample.pdf — template of attestation we will sign after the test

Notes and caveats:
- If you export indexes externally, Redwood cannot purge those external copies. We recommend keeping the index inside Redwood for the duration of the 180d TTL. If you must export, we will include contractual language requiring prompt deletion of exported copies and a joint verification step.
- Purge completion window: we guarantee purge completion events within 72 hours of the deletion action for the Private runtime; the audit trail will show intermediate events.

Next steps: confirm the 10/14 or 10/15 sync time (we proposed 10/14 earlier; if that no longer works, we can do 10/15 at 10am PT). Once we agree, I'll share the Drive link with the artifacts (see link below) and Legal will send DPA amendment draft.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/mediquest/retention-evidence-2026-10

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
